items.context: Round 1 chose 'always a modal dialog' for the ScenarioPicker (d2=B), but components/ui/ has only button, input, section, and error-alert — no dialog primitive. Something must be added. package.json already depends on @radix-ui/react-slot, so @radix-ui/react-dialog is a natural fit. We can also build a minimal custom dialog or adapt an existing pattern.

options.label: Add @radix-ui/react-dialog and wrap it in components/ui/dialog.tsx
options.rationale: Lowest risk and strongest a11y — handles focus trap, Esc to close, scroll lock, portal rendering, and ARIA roles out of the box. Consistent with @radix-ui/react-slot already in tree. Small bundle cost (~10 KB gz).

options.label: Build a minimal custom Dialog with a div, portal, and backdrop
options.rationale: No new dependency and full control over styling. Risk of missing accessibility features (focus trap, aria-modal, keyboard handling) that would need to be added manually. Higher long-term maintenance burden.

options.label: Use @headlessui/react Dialog
options.rationale: Also accessible and well-maintained. Adds a new vendor line alongside the existing Radix dependency, slightly increasing dependency sprawl.

items.topic: Default elements for auto-created assignment on brand creation
items.context: When a user creates a brand with a scenario selected (round-1 d3=A two-call flow), the follow-up POST /api/v1/assignments must specify an 'elements' array (colors, typography, identity, voice, etc.). The user hasn't told us which elements to apply by default for a freshly created brand.

options.label: Apply all available elements by default (colors, typography, identity, voice)
options.rationale: Matches user intent: selecting a scenario at creation means 'make this brand apply to that scenario.' Maximizes value out of the box. User can unassign later if undesired.

options.label: Apply only 'colors' by default
options.rationale: Safest element — always defined on a new brand, never conflicts with scenario content. Lower risk of surprising output. But requires extra clicks to apply the rest.

options.label: Show an element checklist in the picker before assigning
options.rationale: User explicitly chooses what to apply. Most precise but adds another step to the creation flow that most users will skip past.

items.topic: How BrandDetailPage fetches the brand's current scenario assignment
items.context: Repository.AssignmentRepository.ListByBrandID exists but is not exposed over HTTP. BrandDetailPage needs to display the assigned scenario (if any). We need to decide the API surface.

options.label: Add GET /api/v1/brands/{id}/assignments → []Assignment
options.rationale: Directly exposes the existing repository method. Consistent with sibling routes like /brands/{id}/versions and /brands/{id}/assets. Simple to implement and test.

options.label: Embed current assignment in GET /api/v1/brands/{id} response
options.rationale: One fewer request on the detail page. But mutates the brand response shape — risk of breaking existing callers (CLI, tests, any external consumers). Violates the round-1 d3=A 'no contract changes' spirit.

options.label: Have the UI iterate /api/v1/scenarios and filter by brand_id
options.rationale: Reuses the new endpoint. Works today but is O(n) in scenarios per detail-page load and couples the detail page to the full scenario catalog.

items.topic: Reassignment confirmation UX when picking an already-assigned scenario
items.context: Round-1 d4=A allows selecting a scenario that already has a brand assigned, but requires confirmation. We need to decide what that confirmation looks like and what actually happens on the backend — the assignments table has UNIQUE(scenario_name).

options.label: In-dialog confirmation step; on confirm, DELETE the existing assignment then POST the new one
options.rationale: Keeps the two-call flow simple and explicit: delete-then-create. User sees the prior brand name in the confirmation message. Very small race window between delete and create (acceptable for a single-user admin UI).

options.label: In-dialog confirmation, then call a new PATCH /api/v1/assignments/{id} that swaps brand_id atomically
options.rationale: Atomic from the server's perspective. Requires a new API contract and handler. Higher implementation cost for a low-traffic admin action.

options.label: Block reassignment entirely; user must first unassign from the owning brand's detail page
options.rationale: Safest and most explicit. But contradicts round-1 d4=A (user wants reassignment in-flow) and adds friction.

items.text: ApplyPreview (ui/src/components/apply-preview.tsx) currently uses a free-text Input for scenarioName. The plan refactors it to use the new ScenarioPicker — the free-text input is removed, not preserved as a fallback, per the greenfield constraint now pinned at the top of plan.md. Flagging so this refactor isn't missed during implementation.
